To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

electric field induced particle translation in the isotropic as well as in the cholesterical phase of a liquid crystals can be used to create linear as well as rotational motion, whose properties are determined by the electric field strength and frequency.
we investigated the motion of microspheres suspended within a liquid crystal and observed linear, circular and random trajectories.

the translational modes of microspheres suspended within the isotropic and nematic phase of cholesteric liquid crystals depend strongly on applied field amplitude and frequency and that the rotational sense of particles on a circular path in the chiral phase is independent of helicity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of electric-field-induced particle transport in liquid crystalline suspensions, which may have applications for the controlled motion of microparticles in a liquid crystal medium.
a detailed investigation of the stability diagram for electric-field-induced particle transport in a chiral nematic and isotropic liquid crystal.
the electric-field-induced transport of colloidal particles in liquid crystals, and the application of an electric-field-induced transport to microspheres in liquid crystals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the translational dynamics of the microspheres is a result of the interplay of the electric field and the liquid crystalline order, which in turn is influenced by the helicity of this structure.

the translational motion of particles in the isotropic liquid crystalline phase is dominated by the electric field amplitude, whereas in the chiral phase the frequency of the electric field plays the dominant role.

the translational motion of microspheres is a result of the interaction of the applied electric field with the induced dipole moment of the particle and the dielectric anisotropy of the liquid crystal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the translational motion of microspheres can be controlled by the electric field amplitude and the frequency, which allows the application of this system in the field of microfluidics.

electric field-induced translational motion of microspheres suspended within a liquid crystalline host is governed by the same mechanisms in the isotropic phase as well as in the chiral phase of the host.

the translational motion of microspheres suspended within the isotropic phase of a nematic liquid crystal can be described by the electric-field-induced fluid flow model, while the motion within the chiral nematics can be described as a combination of the electric-field-induced flow and the cholesterically driven flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the translational motion of the particles can be controlled by varying the amplitude and the frequency of the applied electric field, and thus the motion can be tuned to be linear or circular.
the electric-field-induced transport of colloidal particles is strongly dependent on the liquid crystalline phase and can be tuned by varying electric field amplitude and applied frequency.

electric field-induced particle translation can be utilized to probe the properties of liquid crystals, and that the motion of particles in the isotropic phase can be used as a tool for studying the chiral nematics.
